newsitem.title: USA: Fed studies role in financial services--Moskow.
newsitem.headline: Fed studies role in financial services--Moskow.

text.p: New technology, banking regulations and competition from the private sector have forced the Federal Reserve to reconsider the scope and type of financial services it provides to the banking sector and the public, Chicago Fed President Michael Moskow said on Thursday.
"Our goal is to enhance the efficiency of the payments system," Moskow told a Bank Administration Institute conference in Fort Lauderdale, Florida. The remarks were made available in New York.
"The best way to increase overall efficiency is to be a first-rate provider of services -- to meet customer needs," Moskow added.

"Ultimately, it's the customer who determines our role. We're required to recover the costs of providing priced services, including the taxes and capital costs the Fed would incur if it were a private firm," Moskow said.
"The key is to adapt to changes in the marketplace. And the best way to do that is to keep in touch with customers," he added.

Moskow acknowledged the Fed "has a long way to go" in terms of adapting to technology and banking industry changes -- though he cited recent improvements to streamline operations in the area of bank examination.
"The Chicago fed has a long way to go. But we're working at it. It's a serious commitment on our part," the bank president stressed.
